submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness is the optimal choice for the RICH detector, delivering 3.8 sigma pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c - the best achievable performance among viable candidates.

The selection process systematically evaluated all three candidates:
- Radiator-R2, despite showing the highest raw separation (4.6 sigma), was eliminated because its porous structure without protective treatment fails the critical humidity ageing constraint
- Radiator-R1 and R3 both pass the ageing requirement and were simulated across the full thickness range (1-6 cm)
- Both R1 and R3 peaked at 3 cm thickness, representing the optimal balance between photon yield and resolution smearing effects
- R3 outperforms R1 by 31% (3.8 vs 2.9 sigma)

R3's hydrophobic treatment ensures transparency loss remains below 10% over the 10-year operational lifetime, meeting the hard constraint that the radiator cannot be replaced during the run. The 3 cm thickness represents the performance optimum, with R3 also showing robust behavior (3.716 sigma at 4 cm), providing tolerance to manufacturing variations.

This recommendation maximizes the physics performance while ensuring long-term detector reliability and compliance with all project constraints.
